The turn timer

Holger, 23 Sep: on the yellow, the ring reads more orange than yellow, and the faded ring is not clear enough. Every version keeps the plates, the number in the plate’s ink and the felt line. Only the ring changes: the arc, the time left, and the track, the faded ring of the time gone.

1 The versions

Each timer stands on the felt at 9, 6 and 3 seconds of a 12 second turn; it turns red for the last five. The fourth timer counts down live when you press Play. The numbers are each colour against the one it must stand out from.

2 How the ring is drawn

On the site (pieces.scss, .spotPrefix-timer) the disc’s background is the fill, an inset 4px box-shadow in --color-timer-ring is the track, an SVG circle’s stroke is the arc, and the number is its own piece (.spotPrefix-timerText). The red state is the .red class, for the last five seconds. The versions change only the track and the arc, so each is two colours per state.

Why both must move. The arc takes #fab005, one step back on the scheme’s yellow walk (#ffd43b, #fcc419, #fab005, #e67700): hue 78, a golden yellow, where #e67700 is hue 55, an orange. The yellow button’s own ring on paper, #f5af23, is the same colour. On today’s track, the plate’s ring #d6b858, that arc would all but vanish (1.04:1), so the track moves too: paler than the fill, a warm grey, or white.
